annotation.title_clean: Opening Speech by Second Minister for Transport Ng Chee Meng for the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill Second Reading
annotation.title_en: Opening Speech by Second Minister for Transport Ng Chee Meng for the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill Second Reading
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Transport, Singapore (Second Minister for Transport Ng Chee Meng)
annotation.summary_en: Ministerial opening speech at the second reading of Singapore's Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill 2017. It introduces a five-year regulatory sandbox for autonomous vehicle trials (SAE levels 3–5) via ministerial rules, and tighter private hire car regulation and penalties, under a balanced light-touch stance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Clause 6 lets the Minister make rules for AV trials and use on public roads, covering time and space limits, equipment design standards and data sharing.
Rules may exempt AVs and operators from human-driver provisions of the Road Traffic Act.
The AV regulatory sandbox is limited to five years, after which permanent legislation or an extension will be considered.
Covers SAE J3016 levels 3, 4 and 5; driver assistance systems are excluded.
Private hire car drivers need vocational licences, and booking operators such as Uber and Grab face duties and suspension orders.
